01 / The foundation02 — 11
First, understand the map

What is graph traversal?

A graph is made of vertices and edges. Traversal means visiting the vertices of a graph in a systematic way.

V

Vertices

The points or nodes in a graph.

E

Edges

The connections between nodes.

Our example graph: 8 vertices and 8 edges.

Both algorithms visit verticesBut in a different order
02 / Breadth-first search03 — 11
Method 01

Breadth-First Search

BFS visits the nearest unvisited neighbours first. It explores the graph level by level.

Remember this rule

FIFO

First In, First Out

The first item added to the queue is the first item removed.

BFS uses a
QUEUE

A queue is a horizontal structure. New items join at the rear; removal happens at the front.

Queue example

FRONT / REMOVEREAR / INSERT
ABCD

A entered first, so A leaves first.

Explore neighbours before going deeperQueue = FIFO

04 / Depth-first search05 — 11
Method 02

Depth-First Search

DFS follows one path as far as possible. When it cannot go further, it goes back and tries another path.

Remember this rule

LIFO

Last In, First Out

The last item added to the stack is the first item removed.

DFS uses a
STACK

A stack is a vertical structure. New items are added and removed at the top.

Stack example

DCBA
TOP / INSERT & REMOVEBOTTOM

D entered last, so D leaves first.

Follow one path, then backtrackStack = LIFO

Same graph, different strategy

BFS vs DFS

PointBFSDFS
StrategyVisits nearby vertices first.Follows one path as far as possible.
Data structureQueueStack
RuleFIFO — First In, First OutLIFO — Last In, First Out

08 / Where they are useful09 — 11
Why do we study them?

Where can we use BFS and DFS?

BFS examples

Explore nearby first

  • Finding the fewest edges between two vertices in an unweighted graph.
  • Finding nearby people or connections in a network.
  • Exploring locations level by level.
DFS examples

Explore a path deeply

  • Exploring paths through a maze.
  • Checking connected parts of a graph.
  • Exploring folder or file structures.

These are examples of where graph traversal ideas can be useful.

ApplicationsDifferent tasks, different strengths
09 / The takeaway10 — 11
In short

Two methods.
One graph.

01

BFS

Explores level by level and uses a horizontal Queue.

02

DFS

Goes deep first and uses a vertical Stack.

↔

Remember

FIFO for Queue. LIFO for Stack.

The best method depends on what we want to explore.
